HOST TESTING GUIDE

One kingdom.
Different ways to thrive.

Choose a council, try a plan, then switch countries to answer proposals. All roles are available to the teacher.

💰 Economy

Manage money and the five resource stocks. Set research and recruitment budgets. Build useful improvements and offer trades.

📚 Research

Choose education and a discovery field, supply its resource kit, and run a local project. Improve a mine, farm, forest camp or weaving workshop, or develop housing and public health. Projects use resources and take time.

🛡 Military

Recruit and assign troops. Click a destination cell and keep a supply path open. Negotiate peace and alliances; decide how to respond when armies meet.

🏡 Shared decisions

All three roles must approve a village or city. Goal cards show prosperity, learning, diplomacy and security routes. Hold the checks for three results in a row.

The turn

🛠 Implement: plan, spend and issue orders → 🤝 Decide: troops move; answer meetings, offers and votes → 📜 Results: see production, discoveries, supplies and battles.

🌾 Food feeds people and troops. 🪵 Wood builds. ⛏ Metal equips and strengthens. 🧵 Cloth supports recruits and development. 💰 Money funds the plans.

Open “Our kingdom goals” above the map to see progress. Select any cell to inspect its production. Country highlighting and zoom help you find your territory. Cities and towns are clickable. Rename a settlement below its cell details; rename a regiment in Military.

Use Save checkpoint before an experiment and Restore turn to undo it. Restoring keeps a backup of the campaign you leave. Download campaigns as durable backups. The version library changes game rules, while checkpoints change the campaign state.

Testing limits: classroom balance is preliminary. No student sign-ins or shared-device synchronization yet. Sea travel and cargo interception along intermediate cells are not included. Imported maps keep geography and diplomacy but receive fresh game population/resources.

🏘 People make the world change

New starter maps already have a named capital and towns. Propose more during Implement; all roles vote in Decide. Existing campaigns keep their established geography and can build more settlements.

People move slowly to neighboring happier places with spare housing. Schools, housing and public health help; shortages, occupation and enemy troops hurt. War closes that border to migration. Use the Happiness and Population & housing map layers, then inspect a cell to see the numbers.

Economy supplies construction and research. R&D chooses which places and resources improve. Military protects supply routes and communities. Each can change the others' opportunities.

Economy sets a separate local R&D allowance from the shared treasury. Research has one local project at a time. Its costs are paid at the start; canceling refunds the unfinished share. Capturing its location cancels the project with no refund. National discoveries continue alongside local projects if their resource kits are available.

GitHub building blocks

These are our integration assessments, based on the linked projects. “Candidate” means adaptable to this JavaScript website, not a ready-made Azgaar plug-in. Only the first two are currently used.

Azgaar Fantasy Map Generator + Battle Simulator · used

Closest fit for biome cells, countries, cities, regiments and battles. We import Full JSON and adapt geography and field-battle phase weights. The game has its own turn, supply and council rules; it does not embed the complete simulator.

D3 Delaunay · used

Builds the starter map's Voronoi cell geometry. Fits the current map and shared-border movement model directly.

boardgame.io · future candidate

Turn-based state management and multiplayer networking. A candidate when student roles and synchronized games become the priority. Would require adapting our rules and adding server hosting for multiplayer; GitHub Pages alone is static.

Graphology · future candidate

Graph data structures and algorithms. Could represent roads, supply networks, city connections and trade routes using cell IDs. Our current graph is small enough for its existing implementation.

Cytoscape.js · future candidate

Interactive network visualization. Could turn research dependencies or resource chains into clickable diagrams for students. It would visualize our rules rather than supply an economy simulation.

Dexie.js · future candidate

IndexedDB wrapper for larger local save libraries and data migrations. Could replace our small checkpoint helper if classroom campaign management grows.

Ajv · future candidate

JSON Schema validation. Could formalize campaign and import formats as the data model settles. Current imports use explicit rule checks.

Phaser · future candidate

Browser game rendering, input, cameras and animation. Useful if animated movement and more elaborate city scenes become important. Adopting it would be a rendering change, not an automatic economy or strategy upgrade.

Economy, settlement benefits, education policies and achievement conditions are deliberately small original rules suited to this classroom game. Each adopted dependency must retain its version and license record.
